title: Make Lua scripting (bevy_mod_scripting/lua54) native-only so the wasm build compiles
description:
## Problem
bevy_mod_scripting 0.21 with the `lua54` feature is currently an unconditional dependency in Cargo.toml. `lua54` builds mlua's bundled Lua C sources, which do not compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, so `trunk build` (the primary distribution target) and the CI `web` job / GitHub Pages deploy fail.

## Approach
Same pattern as the existing avian2d/getrandom target gating (no gameplay changes):
1. Cargo.toml: move `bevy_mod_scripting = { version = "0.21.0", features = ["lua54"] }` out of `[dependencies]` into `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]`.
2. src/main.rs: gate `mod script_manager;` and `.add_plugins(script_manager::ScriptPlugin)` with `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` (or give ScriptPlugin a no-op wasm impl so main.rs stays ungated).
3. Optional: also put it behind a Cargo feature (e.g. `scripting`, default-on) so native builds can opt out with `--no-default-features`. Note that a feature alone isn't enough: trunk would still enable it for wasm unless the dependency is also target-gated.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build` (native) still includes and runs ScriptPlugin/BMSPlugin.
- `trunk build --release` succeeds and the game runs in the browser without scripting.
- CI `native` and `web` jobs are green on master, and the Pages deploy succeeds (https://frederickbrock.github.io/breakout/).
- CLAUDE.md "wasm enablement" note updated to mention scripting is native-only.

title: Game state management: menus, pause, game over
description:
## Problem / goal
The game drops the player straight into play at launch. Introduce proper game-state management: a title/main menu (Start, Settings stub, Quit on native), a working pause menu, and a Game Over / Win screen, built on Bevy States.

## Behaviour
Delivered in three sequenced children: (1) state machine refactor, (2) main menu + Settings screen, (3) pause menu + Game Over/Win screen.

## Out of scope
Real settings (volume/controls/difficulty), audio, high scores, multiple levels, screen transitions/animations, gamepad input.

title: Replace GameStatus with Bevy States and pause physics outside play
description:
## Problem / goal
Replace the hand-checked `GameStatus` resource with a real Bevy state machine as the foundation for menus. No new UI in this task.

## Behaviour
- `AppState { MainMenu, InGame, GameOver }` plus an `InGame` sub-state `PlayState { Playing, Paused }`. In this task the initial state is `InGame` (the menu arrives in the next task).
- Ball, paddle, bricks and HUD spawn when entering `InGame` and are removed when leaving it. Walls and camera stay global.
- Avian's physics clock (`Time<Physics>`) is paused whenever the state is not `InGame/Playing`, and resumed when it is. This replaces the manual velocity-zeroing at game end.
- P or Esc toggles Playing <-> Paused; the existing overlay text shows while paused.
- Losing the last life or clearing all bricks goes to `GameOver`, with a won/lost outcome kept in a resource; the existing text is shown; R starts a new run.
- A new run always resets score to 0 and lives to 3 (one constant); the lives label is driven by that constant. `RestartGame` is still broadcast so power-ups reset themselves.
- Remove the unused `QuitGamme` event.

## Out of scope
Any new menu UI (next tasks), settings, audio.

## Notes for the coder
- `GameStatus` checks to replace: `src/main.rs` (`paddle_movement`, `on_ball_collision`, `ball_movement`, `restart_game`, `update_ui`) and `src/powerups/mod.rs` (3 systems, ~lines 103/143/162). Prefer `run_if(in_state(...))`.
- Keep the `PaddleMovementSet` / `TickActiveEffects` ordering sets working.
- The `RestartGame` observer pattern (`reset_on_restart`) must still fire on every new run.
- Power-up timers must not tick while paused: check what clock `ActiveEffects` ticks on, or gate the tick system.
- Lives today: initial 5 (`insert_resource(Lives(5))`), restart 3, label hard-coded "Lives: 3" — unify on 3.
- Must still build for wasm; don't touch the scripting cfg-gates. Update CLAUDE.md's `GameStatus` notes to describe the state machine.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `cargo build` and `trunk build` both succeed.
- [ ] On launch, the game plays as it does today (ball moves, paddle responds, bricks break, score goes up).
- [ ] Pressing P or Esc while playing freezes the ball, paddle, falling power-ups and active power-up timers and shows the paused text; pressing P or Esc again resumes from the same positions.
- [ ] Losing all lives shows the game-over text and nothing on screen keeps moving.
- [ ] Clearing all bricks shows the win text and nothing on screen keeps moving.
- [ ] Pressing R on the game-over/win screen starts a fresh run: score 0, lives 3, full brick wall, no active power-ups.
- [ ] The HUD shows "Lives: 3" on first launch and after every restart.

title: Add main menu and Settings screen
description:
## Problem / goal
Give the game a title/main menu so the player chooses to start, with a Settings entry that later work will fill in.

## Behaviour
- The app starts in `MainMenu`: title "BREAKOUT" and buttons **Start**, **Settings**, **Quit** (Quit native only; not spawned on wasm). The game world is not visible or simulating behind the menu.
- Start -> `InGame/Playing` with a fresh run (score 0, lives 3).
- Settings -> new `AppState::Settings` screen: heading "Settings", text "Coming soon", a **Back** button returning to the main menu. Esc on Settings also goes back.
- Quit -> exits the app.
- Input: buttons show hover and pressed states under the mouse and respond to clicks. Up/Down or W/S moves a visible focus highlight (wrapping), Enter or Space activates the focused button.
- Button, focus and navigation code lives in a small reusable module `src/menu/` that the pause / game-over task reuses.

## Out of scope
Actual settings, pause menu and game-over screen (next task), gamepad, transitions.

## Notes for the coder
- Bevy UI (`Node`, `Button`, `Interaction`), with screen entities scoped to their state (despawned on exit).
- Quit: `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`, write `AppExit`.
- Builds on the AppState from the previous task; change the initial state to `MainMenu`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Launching (native and web) shows the main menu with Start and Settings, plus Quit on native only; no ball moves behind it.
- [ ] Clicking Start begins a game with score 0 and lives 3.
- [ ] Clicking Settings shows "Settings" / "Coming soon" with a Back button; clicking Back or pressing Esc returns to the main menu.
- [ ] Up/Down (or W/S) visibly moves the highlight between buttons and wraps around; Enter or Space activates the highlighted button.
- [ ] Hovering a button with the mouse changes its appearance.
- [ ] On native, Quit closes the window; the browser build shows no Quit button.
- [ ] `cargo build` and `trunk build` succeed.

title: Add pause menu and Game Over / Win screen
description:
## Problem / goal
Turn the text-only pause and end-of-game overlays into real menus so the player can resume, replay, or return to the title screen.

## Behaviour
- Paused: a menu over the frozen game with title "Paused" and buttons **Resume** and **Main menu**. P or Esc still toggles pause. Main menu abandons the run.
- GameOver: shows "GAME OVER" or "YOU WIN!", the final score, and buttons **Play again** and **Main menu**. R still works as a Play again shortcut.
- Both screens reuse the `src/menu/` module (same mouse + keyboard behaviour as the main menu).

## Out of scope
Restart-from-pause, high scores, transitions/animations.

## Notes for the coder
- Replaces the `GameOverText` overlay strings in `update_ui`.
- Main menu -> MainMenu must fully tear down the run so Start begins fresh (RestartGame still reaches power-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Pressing Esc or P mid-game shows a Paused menu with Resume and Main menu; the game behind it is frozen.
- [ ] Resume (click, Enter, or Esc/P) continues the game exactly where it was.
- [ ] Main menu from pause returns to the title menu; Start from there begins a fresh run (score 0, lives 3, full bricks, no power-ups).
- [ ] Losing shows "GAME OVER" with the final score; winning shows "YOU WIN!" with the final score.
- [ ] Play again (click, Enter, or R) starts a fresh run; Main menu returns to the title screen.
- [ ] `cargo build` and `trunk build` succeed.
